newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL REACH FIRST EURO SEMI SINCE 1985.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL REACH FIRST EURO SEMI SINCE 1985.

text.p: Two goals from Robbie Fowler and one from substitute Stan Collymore gave Liverpool a comprehensive 3-0 victory over Brann Bergen in the second leg of their Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final at Anfield on Thursday.
And Liverpool's 4-1 aggregate victory gave them a place in a European semifinal for the first time in 12 years which their dominance thoroughly warranted.

Fowler opened the scoring with a 25th minute penalty, Collymore bulldozed his way through the centre of the Norwegian defence to make it 2-0 in the 62nd - two minutes after replacing Czech Patrick Berger - and Fowler added the third in the 78th minute with a low shot into the far corner of the net.

Brann, bidding to become the first Norwegian club ever to reach a European semifinal, rarely troubled the Liverpool defence in which Mark Wright and Steve Harkness were outstanding. Dominic Matteo was also a commanding presence at the back in the first half before injury forced him off at half- time.

John Barnes, Jamie Redknapp and Steve McManaman also had particularly good games for the home side, who were only denied a bigger winning margin because of wasted chances in front of goal -- and some good goalkeeping from 33-veteran reserve Vidar Bahus.
